title: docs(i18n): the README's built-in locale count is ten, and derived rather than restated (objectui#7989)
body:
Fixes #7989

`packages/i18n/README.md` claimed **11** built-in locales in the two places a reader meets
first, and hedged the list with "and more". The package ships **10**, and the same document
already reasons correctly on ten six times further down. That README is in the package's
`files`, so the wrong number went out in every tarball.

## What this does

Two lines corrected, and then the construct that permitted the error removed:

- `README.md:3` and `:7` state **10**, and the `and more` hedge is gone — that bullet
  enumerates all ten languages, so there was no more.
- A new pin **derives** the number instead of letting the prose restate it.

Correcting alone was weighed and refused. objectui#3351 is the same off-by-one in a
changeset file ("eleven locale packs — the repo has ten"); it was fixed **in isolation**,
nobody swept the README, and the README is why this card exists. A restated number rots
again on the next pack, and objectui#7479 / objectui#7486 are actively reshaping how the
packs load.

## The pin asserts two published doors and asserts they agree

The card's recipe no longer runs. objectui#7479 removed the `builtInLocales` re-export from
the package **entry** — an object literal naming ten catalogue modules is the one shape no
bundler can shake — so `import { builtInLocales } from '@object-ui/i18n'` fails today. What
a consumer of `.` gets is `BUILT_IN_LANGUAGE_CODES` at zero payload; the map is behind the
published `@object-ui/i18n/locales` subpath.

Both are asserted, and asserted to **agree**. The agreement leg is the load-bearing one: a
pack registered but never exported, or exported but never registered, moves one instrument
and not the other, and a README pinned to only one would stay green over a package that
disagrees with itself.

⛔ Deliberately **not** a third instrument: the `.ts` file count under `src/locales/`. That
directory holds 13 files and 10 of them are packs — `index.ts`, `registry.ts` and `rtl.ts`
are not locales. Counting files reproduces the very error this pin exists to stop, and the
non-pack count has already grown from one to three since triage measured it.

## Proof that the pin can fail

Ablated twice. Each leg mutates, proves the mutation reached disk by anchor counts **and**
by `git hash-object` differing from the `HEAD` blob, runs, then restores from an
`EXIT`/`INT`/`TERM` trap with `git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH` and proves restoration by
**state** (`git diff HEAD` empty, hash back to `96455b93d`), never by an exit code.

| mutation | result |
| --- | --- |
| count reverted to 11 | FAIL `is what the one-line description restates` — expected 11 to be 10 |
| `and more` hedge restored | FAIL `is how many languages the feature bullet actually enumerates, with no hedge` — expected length 10, got 11 |

## The ledger entry, and the concurrency

A test that reads **any** markdown document owes an `ADJUDICATED` entry in
`scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs`. Reading its own package's README is no exception: that
ledger is keyed by test file, not by whether the read escapes a package, and eleven entries
already in the Map are this exact shape. Without the entry the audit reports
`unadjudicated-test` and `scripts/__tests__/markdown-test-inputs.test.ts` fails — correctly,
because `ci.yml` would otherwise be unable to tell that editing this README edits a test's
input, and a markdown-only pull request would skip the shard.

⚠️ This pull request and objectui#9602 both add an entry to that same `ADJUDICATED` Map.
This is a **measured non-conflict**, not an absence of interaction: the entries sort to
lines 310 and 493 of the merged file, and `git merge-tree --write-tree` run against
objectui#9602's head (`e6d0d38`) exits **0** and writes a tree that contains **both**
entries. Whichever lands second merges without a conflict.

## Gates

| gate | exit |
| --- | --- |
| `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --audit` | 0 — 98 candidates, all adjudicated; 73 entries, all present |
| `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/markdown-test-inputs.test.ts` + the pin | 0 — 2 files, 28 tests |
| every other test naming the edited script | 0 — 4 files, 77 tests |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/i18n/` | 0 — 68 files, 1129 tests |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/i18n type-check` | 0 (after building the dependency closure) |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/i18n lint` | 0 (33 pre-existing warnings, 0 errors) |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | 0 |
| `check-changeset-no-major` · `check-changeset-fixed` · `check-control-bytes` | 0 |
| `check-doc-links` · `check-doc-fence-languages` · `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` | 0 |
| `check-test-path-roots` · `check-vi-mock-specifiers` | 0 |
| `check-governed-queue-guard --test` | NOT GOVERNED — ordinary review and merge-queue route |

Exit codes were captured on their own line after a redirect, never read after a pipe.
Repo-wide scans (`pnpm lint`, `pnpm type-check`, the full `pnpm test`) are CI's run, not
claimed here.

## Acceptance notes

Observed while measuring, deliberately **not** repaired here:

- The same wrong count sits in six places outside this README — one of them a docblock in
  the published source of a different package, the rest in `ROADMAP.md`, three of which say
  11 and then enumerate ten codes on the same line. Reported to the dispatching seat and
  being filed on its own card. ⛔ Out of scope for a card about one README.
- `of the ten packs.` has moved from `README.md:175` to `:266` since triage measured it.
  The claim is intact; a line citation in a comment aged.
- `src/index.ts` and `package.json` both say `10+` where the figure is exactly 10. Both are
  correct and both are untouched — fixing what is right is how a documentation card grows.
